title: Cart Conditions
description: Comprehensive guide to setting up complex and advanced cart conditions for discount rules
content: ## Cart Conditions Conditions are one of the most powerful tools in the discount rules system. They allow you to define **when** a discount rule will be activated, based on the customer's cart content. ### What are Conditions? **Conditions** are requirements that customers must meet for the rule to activate: **Examples:** * "Cart must contain at least $200" * "Customer must purchase at least 3 items" * "Electronics subtotal must be over $500" **Without Conditions** = Rule always applies (if Filters exist, it applies to filtered products). Conditions check **cart content**. Filters check **product attributes**. They're not the same! This is a critical point to understand: | | **Filters** | **Conditions** | |---|-------------|----------------| | **Asks** | "**Which** products?" | "**When** to activate?" | | **Checks** | Product attributes | Cart content | | **Example** | "Only shirts" | "Over $200" | | **Effect** | Which products get discount | Whether rule activates at all | **Practical Example:** ``` Promotion: 20% off shirts when purchasing over $300 Filters: Categories → Include → "Shirts" ↳ Discount applies only to shirts Conditions: Subtotal (cart) ≥ 300 ↳ Rule activates only if cart total is over $300 ``` **Result:** * Cart with shirts at $200 → ❌ No discount (doesn't meet condition) * Cart with shirts at $400 → ✅ 20% off shirts * Cart with shirts $100 + shoes $250 → ✅ 20% off shirts only *** ## Types of Conditions The system supports 4 main condition types: **Definition:** Total amount of all products in cart (before discounts and shipping) **When to use:** * Free shipping over amount * General discount for large carts * Encourage cart size increase **Examples:** * Subtotal (cart) **≥ 200** = "Over $200" * Subtotal (cart) **≤ 500** = "Up to $500" * Subtotal (cart) **= 100** = "Exactly $100" **Practical Example:** ``` Name: "Free Shipping Over $200" Type: Shipping discount Settings: 100% discount on shipping Filters: None Conditions: Subtotal (cart) ≥ 200 ``` **Definition:** Amount of products from specific category/categories in cart **When to use:** * Promotion on specific category with amount condition * "Buy X from category Y over amount Z" * Encourage purchasing from specific category **Fields:** * **Condition Type:** Category subtotal * **Compare:** Comparison operator (≥, ≤, =, etc.) * **Values:** Category selection * **Amount:** Required amount **Examples:** ``` Category subtotal Categories: "Electronics" Compare: ≥ Amount: 500 = "Electronics amount in cart must be over $500" ``` **Practical Example:** ``` Name: "$50 off shoes when buying over $400 in shoes" Type: Product adjustment Settings: $50 discount Filters: Categories → Include → "Shoes" Conditions: - Type: Category subtotal - Categories: "Shoes" - Compare: ≥ - Amount: 400 ``` **Definition:** Amount from specific products you selected in cart **When to use:** * Promotion on specific products with amount condition * "Buy products X,Y,Z over amount" * Bundle deals on selected products **Fields:** * **Condition Type:** Products subtotal * **Compare:** Comparison operator * **Values:** Specific product selection * **Amount:** Required amount **Examples:** ``` Products subtotal Products: "HP Laptop", "Dell Laptop" Compare: ≥ Amount: 3000 = "Selected laptops amount in cart over $3000" ``` **Practical Example:** ``` Name: "Buy Apple products over $5000 and get headphones free" Type: BXGY Settings: Buy: Apple products Get: Headphones (100% discount) Filters: None Conditions: - Type: Products subtotal - Products: "iPhone 15", "MacBook Pro", "iPad" - Compare: ≥ - Amount: 5000 ``` **Definition:** Number of different items in cart (not total quantity!) **When to use:** * "Buy X different items" * Encourage cart variety * Promotions on item quantity **Important to understand:** * Counts by **number of lines** in cart * 3 shirts of same product = **1 item** * 3 different shirts = **3 items** **Examples:** ``` Line Item Count ≥ 3 = "At least 3 different products in cart" ``` **Practical Example:** ``` Name: "Buy 5 different products and get 10% off" Type: Cart adjustment Settings: 10% discount Filters: None Conditions: Line Item Count ≥ 5 ``` If you want to count unit quantity (not different products), use Bulk Discount instead of Conditions. *** ## Comparison Operators Each condition uses a comparison operator: | Symbol | Meaning | Example | Explanation | |--------|---------|---------|-------------| | **↑=** | Greater or equal | ≥ 200 | Over 200 or exactly 200 | | **↓=** | Less or equal | ≤ 500 | Up to 500 including | | **↑** | Greater than | > 100 | Over 100 (not including 100) | | **↓** | Less than | \< 1000 | Under 1000 (not including) | | **=** | Equal to | = 50 | Exactly 50 | | **=X** | Not equal to | ≠ 0 | Any value except 0 | **Tips:** * ✅ Use **≥** (greater or equal) for most cases - "over $200" * ✅ Use **≤** (less or equal) for limited promotions - "up to $500" * ⚠️ Be careful with **=** (exactly equal) - rarely needed *** ## Match ALL vs Match ANY When you have more than one condition, you need to choose the logic: **Definition:** Customer must meet **all** conditions you defined **When to use:** * When multiple requirements are mandatory * Complex promotions with several conditions * When you want to be strict **Example:** ``` Match ALL: 1. Subtotal (cart) ≥ 300 2. Line Item Count ≥ 3 Meaning: Customer needs to purchase over $300 **and** at least 3 different products ``` **Scenarios:** | Amount | Items | Result | |--------|-------|--------| | $350 | 4 items | ✅ Meets both | | $400 | 2 items | ❌ Not enough items | | $250 | 5 items | ❌ Not enough amount | **Definition:** Customer needs to meet **at least one** of the conditions **When to use:** * When there are multiple ways to earn discount * Flexible promotions * When you want to give customers options **Example:** ``` Match ANY: 1. Subtotal (cart) ≥ 500 2. Line Item Count ≥ 5 Meaning: Customer needs to purchase over $500 **or** at least 5 different products ``` **Scenarios:** | Amount | Items | Result | |--------|-------|--------| | $600 | 2 items | ✅ Meets amount | | $300 | 7 items | ✅ Meets items | | $400 | 4 items | ❌ Meets neither | *** ## Practical Examples **Goal:** Free shipping for anyone purchasing over $200 ``` Name: "Free Shipping Over $200" Type: Shipping discount Settings: 100% discount Filters: None Conditions: Logic: Match ALL (doesn't matter, only one condition) - Subtotal (cart) ≥ 200 ``` **How it works:** * Customer with $150 cart → ❌ Pays for shipping * Customer with $250 cart → ✅ Free shipping **Goal:** 20% off electronics when purchasing over $1000 in electronics ``` Name: "20% off electronics over $1000" Type: Product adjustment Settings: 20% discount Filters: - Categories → Include → "Electronics" Conditions: Logic: Match ALL - Type: Category subtotal - Categories: "Electronics" - Compare: ≥ - Amount: 1000 ``` **How it works:** * Cart: Laptop $800 → ❌ No discount (didn't reach $1000) * Cart: Laptop $800 + Mouse $250 → ✅ 20% off both * Cart: Laptop $1200 + Shoes $300 → ✅ 20% off laptop only **Goal:** 15% discount when purchasing over $400 **and** at least 3 different products ``` Name: "15% discount - $400 + 3 items" Type: Cart adjustment Settings: 15% discount Filters: None Conditions: Logic: Match ALL (must meet both!) 1. Subtotal (cart) ≥ 400 2. Line Item Count ≥ 3 ``` **How it works:** | Cart | Amount | Items | Result | |------|--------|-------|--------| | 3 different shirts + pants | $450 | 4 | ✅ 15% discount | | 5 identical shirts | $500 | 1 | ❌ No discount | | 2 items | $600 | 2 | ❌ No discount | **Goal:** 10% discount for purchasing over $500 **or** at least 5 items ``` Name: "10% discount - $500 or 5 items" Type: Cart adjustment Settings: 10% discount Filters: None Conditions: Logic: Match ANY (one is enough) 1. Subtotal (cart) ≥ 500 2. Line Item Count ≥ 5 ``` **How it works:** | Cart | Amount | Items | Result | |------|--------|-------|--------| | 6 cheap items | $300 | 6 | ✅ 10% discount (meets items) | | One expensive item | $700 | 1 | ✅ 10% discount (meets amount) | | 3 items | $400 | 3 | ❌ No discount (meets neither) | **Goal:** Free shipping for purchasing: * Over $300 general **or** * Over $200 in electronics **or** * At least 4 sports products ``` Name: "Free shipping - 3 flexible conditions" Type: Shipping discount Settings: 100% discount Filters: None Conditions: Logic: Match ANY (one is enough) 1. Subtotal (cart) ≥ 300 2. Category subtotal → "Electronics" ≥ 200 3. Products subtotal → Sports products ≥ 4 items ``` **How it works:** * Cart: $350 general → ✅ Free shipping (condition 1) * Cart: Laptop $250 + Book $50 → ✅ Free shipping (condition 2) * Cart: 4 balls $150 → ✅ Free shipping (condition 3) * Cart: $250 regular products → ❌ Pays shipping *** ## Advanced Combinations Real power comes from proper combination of Filters and Conditions: **Example 1: Targeted Discount** ``` Goal: 30% off children's clothing when purchasing over $200 in clothing Filters: - Categories → Include → "Children's Clothing" Conditions: - Category subtotal → "Children's Clothing", "Baby Clothing" ≥ 200 ``` **Example 2: Conditional BOGO** ``` Goal: Buy 2 shirts get 1 free - only for carts over $150 Type: BOGO Settings: Buy 2, Get 1 (100%) Filters: - Categories → Include → "Shirts" Conditions: - Subtotal (cart) ≥ 150 ``` You can create discount tiers using multiple rules: ``` Rule 1: "5% over $200" Priority: 20 Type: Cart adjustment Settings: 5% Conditions: Subtotal ≥ 200 Rule 2: "10% over $500" Priority: 10 Type: Cart adjustment Settings: 10% Conditions: Subtotal ≥ 500 Rule 3: "15% over $1000" Priority: 0 Type: Cart adjustment Settings: 15% Conditions: Subtotal ≥ 1000 ``` **Result:** * $150 → No discount * $300 → 5% discount * $700 → 10% discount * $1500 → 15% discount *** ## Tips and Best Practices **Don't complicate immediately:** * Start with one condition * Test that it works * Add more conditions gradually **Progress example:** ``` Step 1: No Conditions ↓ Tested, works Step 2: + Subtotal ≥ 200 ↓ Tested, works Step 3: + Line Item Count ≥ 3 ↓ Tested, works - Done! ``` **Before launch:** 1. Create cart exactly as customer would 2. Check discount appears/doesn't appear correctly 3. Try edge cases: * Exactly on threshold ($199.99 vs $200) * Below threshold * Way above threshold **Edge cases to test:** ``` If condition: Subtotal ≥ 200 Test: ✅ $199 → No discount ✅ $200 → Has discount ✅ $201 → Has discount ✅ $500 → Has discount ``` **Common problem:** Two conditions that can't both be true **Problem example:** ``` ❌ Wrong: Match ALL: 1. Subtotal (cart) ≥ 500 2. Subtotal (cart) ≤ 300 ↳ No cart will meet both conditions! ``` **Solution:** ``` ✅ Correct: Match ALL: 1. Subtotal (cart) ≥ 300 2. Subtotal (cart) ≤ 500 ↳ Carts between $300-$500 ``` **In Message field or rule name:** * Explain what the rule should do * Document conditions in plain language * This will help you in the future **Good example:** ``` Name: "Free shipping over $200 - until 12/31" Message: "You got free shipping! Keep shopping over $200" ``` **Rule of thumb:** **Match ALL** when: * All conditions are mandatory * Want to be strict * Expensive/limited promotion **Match ANY** when: * Multiple ways to qualify * Want to be flexible * Broad promotion **Example:** ``` Match ALL: "Over $500 **and** 5 items" ↳ Strict - only large customers Match ANY: "Over $500 **or** 5 items" ↳ Flexible - more customers qualify ``` *** ## Frequently Asked Questions **No!** Conditions are optional: * **Without Conditions** = Rule always applies * **With Conditions** = Rule applies only when conditions are met **When you don't need Conditions:** * Simple category discount (Filters are enough) * BOGO without restrictions * General site-wide promotion **Category subtotal:** * Amount from entire category * Example: All "Electronics" products **Products subtotal:** * Amount from specific products you selected * Example: Only "iPhone 15" and "iPad Pro" **When to use each:** * Category = When there are many products in category * Products = When you want precise control over specific products **Yes! And recommended!** This is the most powerful combination: * **Filters** = Which products * **Conditions** = When to activate **Example:** ``` Promotion: 20% off clothing when purchasing over $300 Filters: Categories → "Clothing" ↳ Discount only on clothing Conditions: Subtotal (cart) ≥ 300 ↳ Rule activates only over $300 ``` **Simply - rule doesn't apply:** * No discount * No message * Rule just ignores the cart **Customer doesn't know:** * That such rule exists * That they almost met condition * How much is missing **Tip:** Use Message to encourage: ``` Message: "$50 more and you'll get free shipping!" ``` **Yes, but:** * ✅ Can add many conditions * ⚠️ Keep it simple - easier to manage * ⚠️ Test thoroughly - more conditions = more room for errors **Recommendation:** * Up to 3 conditions = Excellent * 4-5 conditions = OK but test well * 6+ conditions = Consider splitting into multiple rules *** ## Summary **Conditions are a powerful tool for creating smart promotions:** 🎯 **4 Condition Types:** 1. Subtotal (cart) - Cart amount 2. Category subtotal - Amount from category 3. Products subtotal - Amount from specific products 4. Line Item Count - Number of different items 🔧 **2 Logic Modes:** * Match ALL - Meet all conditions * Match ANY - Meet at least one condition 💡 **Guiding Principles:** * Start simple * Test in real cart * Combine with Filters for maximum power * Document intent **Remember:** Filters = "Which products", Conditions = "When" *** ### Continue Reading

title: Creating Discount Rules
description: Step-by-step guide to creating new discount rules in Whizmanage system
content: ## Creating a New Discount Rule Creating a new discount rule in the Whizmanage system is a simple and intuitive process. In this guide, we'll go through all the steps required to create a professional and functional discount rule. ### Quick Start 1. Navigate to the **Discounts** tab in the side menu 2. Click the **Add rule** button in the top right corner 3. Select **Create new rule** from the dropdown menu Alternatively, you can click **Duplicate** next to an existing rule to copy it and edit the details. The form is divided into three main sections: **Left side:** * Rule details * Schedule **Right side:** * Filters (product filtering) * Conditions (cart conditions) ### Step 1: Basic Rule Details **Rule name** - A descriptive name to help you identify the rule: ✅ **Good names:** * "Summer Sale 2024 - 20% Sitewide" * "BOGO on Shirts - July" * "Free Shipping Over $200" ❌ **Not recommended:** * "Discount 1" * "test" * "New rule" Use names that describe the promotion, dates, and conditions. This will help you find and manage rules easily. **Discount type** - Choose the appropriate discount type for your promotion: | Type | When to Use | |------|-------------| | **Product adjustment** | Uniform discount on specific products | | **Cart adjustment** | Discount on entire cart | | **Bulk discount** | Tiered discounts by quantity | | **BOGO** | Buy X Get Y same product | | **BXGY** | Buy product X Get product Y | | **Shipping discount** | Discount on shipping cost | | **Spend bundle** | Bundle deals | Click the **settings button** (⚙️) next to the discount type: **For Product/Cart Adjustment:** * **Discount method:** Percentage (%) or fixed amount ($) * **Discount value:** The amount or percentage * **Maximum discount:** (Optional) Limit maximum discount amount * **Create coupon:** Whether to create an automatic coupon displayed in cart Each discount type displays different settings. For example, BOGO shows X and Y quantity fields, and Bulk Discount shows a tier table. **Status** - Rule state: * **Active** - Rule is active and running * **Draft** - Rule is not active **Priority** - Number determining execution order: * **Lower** value = **Higher** priority * Default: 0 * Useful when multiple rules can apply to the same product If there's a rule with Priority=0 (20% discount) and a rule with Priority=10 (10% discount), the Priority=0 rule will execute first. ### Step 2: Rule Scheduling **Schedule (optional)** - Determine when the rule will be active: **Start date** - Start date and time: * Leave empty = active immediately * Set future date for scheduled promotions **End date** - End date and time: * Leave empty = no time limit * Set end date for temporary promotions It's recommended to set end dates for special promotions to prevent them from staying active by mistake. ### Step 3: Setting Filters (Product Filtering) Filters determine **which products** the rule applies to. 1. On the right side, in the **Filters** section, click **Add filter** 2. Select the filter type: * **Categories** - Product categories * **Tags** - Product tags * **Attributes** - Attributes (color, size, etc.) * **Products** - Specific products * **On Sale** - Products on sale **Mode** - Filtering method: * **Include** - Include only selected values * **Exclude** - Exclude selected values **Values** - Select values: * Start typing to search * Select one or more values * Can select multiple categories/tags/products **Scenario:** Discount only on electronics * Field: **Categories** * Mode: **Include** * Values: **Electronics, Computers** You can add multiple filters that work together: **Complex example:** 1. Categories → Include → "Clothing" 2. Tags → Exclude → "Sale" 3. Attributes → Include → Color: "Red" **Meaning:** Rule applies only to red clothing not on sale. ### Step 4: Setting Conditions (Cart Conditions) Conditions determine **when** the rule activates based on cart contents. Select the logic: **Match ALL** - Customer must meet all conditions * Useful for complex promotions with multiple requirements **Match ANY** - Customer needs to meet at least one condition * Useful for promotions with multiple benefit options 1. Click **Add Condition** 2. Select **Condition Type**: * **Subtotal (cart)** - Total cart amount * **Category subtotal** - Amount from specific category * **Products subtotal** - Amount from specific products * **Line Item Count** - Number of different items **Compare** - Choose the comparison method: | Symbol | Meaning | Example | |--------|---------|---------| | ↑= | Greater or equal | ≥ 200 | | ↓= | Less or equal | ≤ 500 | | ↑ | Greater than | > 100 | | ↓ | Less than | \< 1000 | | = | Equal to | = 50 | | =X | Not equal to | ≠ 0 | For **Category subtotal** or **Products subtotal**: * Select relevant categories or products * Can select multiple categories/products **Amount** - The amount or quantity: * For Subtotal: Amount in currency * For Item Count: Number of items **Promotion:** Free shipping over $200 for shoe purchases **Condition:** * Type: **Category subtotal** * Compare: **↑=** (greater or equal) * Values: **Shoes** * Amount: **200** ### Step 5: Adding Customer Message (Optional) **Message** - Text displayed to customer in cart: * Explain the discount * Encourage purchase completion * Promotion details **Examples:** * "You got 20% off all products! 🎉" * "Free shipping thanks to your purchase over $200" * "Special offer: Buy 2 Get 1 Free" ### Step 6: Saving and Testing 1. Click **Save** in the bottom left corner 2. System will validate and check required fields 3. If everything is correct, rule will be saved and appear in table * **"Rule name is required"** - Must enter rule name * **"Please select values"** - Must select values in Filters/Conditions that require selection * **"End date must be after start date"** - End date must be after start date After saving the rule, it's recommended to test: ✅ **Basic test:** 1. Add relevant product to cart 2. Verify discount appears 3. Check customer message ✅ **Testing conditions:** 1. Add products until reaching minimum amount 2. Verify discount activates only when conditions are met 3. Test different scenarios (below/above threshold) ✅ **Testing filters:** 1. Add products included in Filters 2. Add products not included 3. Verify discount applies only to correct products ### Complete Examples **Goal:** 15% discount on all electronics **Settings:** * **Name:** "Electronics 15% Discount" * **Type:** Product adjustment * **Settings:** 15% discount * **Status:** Active * **Priority:** 0 **Filters:** * Categories → Include → "Electronics" **Conditions:** (none) **Goal:** Free shipping over $300 **Settings:** * **Name:** "Free Shipping Over $300" * **Type:** Shipping discount * **Settings:** 100% discount on shipping * **Status:** Active **Filters:** (none) **Conditions:** * Type: Subtotal (cart) * Compare: ≥ * Amount: 300 **Goal:** Buy 2 shirts get 1 free **Settings:** * **Name:** "BOGO Shirts" * **Type:** BOGO * **Settings:** Buy 2, Get 1 free (100%) * **Status:** Active **Filters:** * Categories → Include → "Shirts" **Conditions:** (none) ### Recommended Tips 1. **Start simple** - Create a simple rule and test it before adding complex conditions 2. **Use descriptive names** - This will help you find and manage rules 3. **Set end dates** - Prevent promotions from staying active by mistake 4. **Test in staging** - Before activating in live store 5. **Document** - Note what each rule should do ### Continue Reading

title: Discount Rules
description: Powerful and flexible system for managing advanced discounts in your WooCommerce store
content: ## Discount Rules - Advanced Promotions Management Whizmanage's Discount Rules system allows you to create and manage complex, advanced discount promotions with ease. With an intuitive interface and powerful tools, you can define custom discounts that perfectly match your sales strategy. ### What are Discount Rules? Discount rules are automatic rules that apply discounts to products or shopping carts based on conditions you define. Unlike regular coupons, discount rules work automatically without requiring a code entry. With discount rules you can create: * Tiered discounts based on purchase quantity * BOGO (Buy X Get Y) promotions * Discounts on specific categories * Discounts conditional on cart value * Free shipping under conditions The advanced table interface allows: * Quick editing of rules directly in the table * Easy filtering and searching of rules * Bulk editing of multiple rules * Duplicating existing rules * Tracking status and schedules Precise control over discounts: * Start and end dates * Priority between rules * Custom conditions * Limiting to specific products * Combining cart and product conditions ### Discount Rule Types The system supports a wide variety of discount types: 1. **Product Adjustment** - Discount on specific products 2. **Cart Adjustment** - Discount on entire cart 3. **Bulk Discount** - Tiered discounts by quantity 4. **BOGO** - Buy X Get Y (same product) 5. **BXGY** - Buy X Get Y (different products) 6. **Shipping Discount** - Discount on shipping 7. **Spend Bundle** - Bundle deals Each discount type comes with its own dedicated settings. For example, BOGO allows you to set different quantities and products for purchase and gift. ### Basic Rule Components Every discount rule consists of several main components: **Rule Name** - A descriptive name that helps you identify the rule **Discount Type** - Select the appropriate discount type (Product, Cart, BOGO, etc.) **Discount Settings** - The settings button allows you to configure the discount method, percentages, fixed amounts, and more Filters allow you to limit the rule to specific products: * **Categories** - Include or exclude categories * **Tags** - Filter by product tags * **Attributes** - Filter by attributes like color, size * **Specific Products** - Manual product selection * **On Sale** - Only sale products or vice versa Filters determine **which products** the rule applies to. If no Filters are set, the rule applies to all products. Conditions determine **when** the rule will activate based on cart contents: * **Subtotal** - Minimum cart amount * **Category Subtotal** - Amount from specific category * **Products Subtotal** - Amount from specific products * **Item Count** - Number of items in cart Each condition includes: * **Condition Type** - Cart, category, products * **Comparison Operator** - Greater than, less than, equal * **Value** - The required amount or quantity You can set multiple conditions and choose whether the customer needs to meet all conditions (Match ALL) or at least one (Match ANY). **Dates** - Set the rule's active period: * Start date * End date * Leave empty = no time limit **Priority** - Number that determines rule application order when multiple rules are relevant. Lower value = higher priority. **Status** - Quick enable/disable of the rule: * 🟢 Active * ⚫ Draft ### Difference Between Filters and Conditions This is one of the important things to understand: | Aspect | Filters | Conditions | |--------|---------|------------| | **Purpose** | Determine **which products** the rule applies to | Determine **when** the rule activates | | **Based On** | Product attributes (category, tag, SKU) | Cart contents (amount, quantity) | | **Example** | "Only products from clothing category" | "When cart total exceeds $100" | | **Default** | All products | All carts | **Scenario:** 20% discount on clothing when purchasing over $200 * **Filters:** Category = "Clothing" (only clothing gets discount) * **Conditions:** Subtotal ≥ 200 (rule only activates if cart exceeds $200) ### Advanced Features Edit multiple rules at once: * Change dates for all rules * Update priorities * Change status * Update discount settings Create new versions of existing rules quickly: * Duplicate rule with one click * Edit unique details * Save time configuring similar rules The system maintains change history: * Undo recent changes * Redo undone changes * Safer workflow ### Continue Reading

title: Managing Discount Rules
description: Tips and techniques for efficient management of discount rules in Whizmanage system
content: ## Managing and Organizing Discount Rules Efficient management of discount rules is crucial for running successful promotions. In this guide, we'll learn how to leverage all the tools the system offers for professional and efficient management. ### Table Interface The discount rules table displays consolidated information about all rules: **Main columns:** * **Name** - Rule name * **Type** - Discount type + settings button * **Status** - Enable/disable toggle * **Start/End date** - Active dates * **Priority** - Priority order * **Filters** - Product filtering + edit button * **Conditions** - Cart conditions + edit button * **Message** - Customer message You can change column widths by dragging the dividing line between column headers. Most fields are editable directly in the table: **Single click:** * **Name** - Edit rule name * **Priority** - Change priority number * **Message** - Edit message * **Start/End date** - Change dates **Toggles:** * **Status** - Instant enable/disable of rule **Edit buttons:** * **Type Settings** (⚙️) - Open discount settings * **Filters Edit** - Edit product filters * **Conditions Edit** - Edit cart conditions Every change is saved automatically after editing. No need to click a "Save" button. ### Filtering and Search Tools The search field at the top of the table allows: * Search by rule name * Search by discount type * Search by message * Instant results while typing **Search examples:** * "summer" - will find all rules with the word summer * "BOGO" - will find BOGO rules * "shipping" - will find free shipping rules The **Filters** button allows quick filtering: **Status:** * 🟢 **Active** - Only active rules * ⚫ **Draft** - Only drafts * 🔄 **All** - All rules **Type:** * **Product adjustment** * **Cart adjustment** * **BOGO** * **BXGY** * And more... Combine text search with filters for more precise results. For example: search "summer" + filter Status:Active. Clicking on a column header sorts the table: **Useful sorts:** * **Priority** - To see rules in execution order * **Start date** - To see rules by start date * **End date** - To find rules expiring soon * **Name** - Alphabetical sort **Sort direction:** * ↑ Ascending (A→Z, 0→9, old→new) * ↓ Descending (Z→A, 9→0, new→old) ### Bulk Edit **Manual selection:** 1. Check the checkbox next to each rule 2. Or click the checkbox in the header to select all **Number of selected rules** appears in the bar at the bottom of the screen. When rules are selected, a **Floating Toolbar** appears at the bottom with options: **Available actions:** * 📋 **Duplicate** - Duplicate selected rules * ⚙️ **Bulk Edit** - Bulk editing * 🗑️ **Move to Trash** - Move to trash * ♻️ **Restore** (in trash) - Restore rules * 🔴 **Delete Permanently** - Permanent deletion **Duplicate** action for more than one rule is available only in Pro version. **Bulk Edit** allows editing multiple rules simultaneously: 1. Select desired rules 2. Click **Bulk Edit** from Toolbar 3. Choose fields to edit: * **Status** - Change status for all * **Priority** - Increase/decrease priority * **Start/End date** - Update dates * **Message** - Replace message 4. Set new values 5. Click **Apply Changes** **Useful scenarios:** * Extend promotion - Update End date for all rules * Temporary disable - Change Status to Draft * Update priorities - Increase Priority by 10 ### Duplicating Rules Duplicating a rule is the fastest way to create a similar rule: 1. Select one rule 2. Click **Duplicate** in Toolbar 3. Rule will be duplicated with "(copy)" added to name 4. Edit the duplicated rule as needed **What's duplicated:** * All settings and parameters * Filters * Conditions * Dates (same as original) **What changes:** * Status changes to **Draft** * "(copy)" added to name After duplicating, it's recommended to change dates and name immediately to avoid confusion. Duplicating multiple rules at once (Pro): 1. Select multiple rules 2. Click **Duplicate** 3. All rules will be duplicated with "(copy)" 4. Edit using Bulk Edit **Useful for:** * Creating series of similar promotions * Copying rules to new cycle * Creating variations of same promotion ### Undo/Redo The system automatically maintains change history: **Undo/Redo buttons** at top of table: * ↶ **Undo** - Cancel last change * ↷ **Redo** - Restore canceled change **Keyboard shortcuts:** * `Ctrl+Z` (Windows) / `Cmd+Z` (Mac) - Undo * `Ctrl+Y` (Windows) / `Cmd+Shift+Z` (Mac) - Redo History is saved only in current session. Page refresh will clear history. Almost any action can be undone: * ✅ Field editing * ✅ Status change * ✅ Date updates * ✅ Filters/Conditions changes * ✅ Bulk Edit * ✅ Creating new rule * ❌ Permanent deletion (Delete Permanently) ### Column Management The **Columns** button at top of table allows: **Show/hide columns:** * Check/uncheck columns * Columns update immediately * Settings saved automatically **Useful for:** * Focused display of relevant information * Working on small screens * Simplifying interface It's recommended to hide columns you don't regularly use to simplify the view. You can change the order of columns in the table: 1. Drag column header 2. Drop at desired location 3. New order saved automatically Columns can be pinned to table sides: **Pinned columns:** * **Left:** Actions, Select, Expand * **Right:** Row actions **Benefits:** * Convenient horizontal scrolling * Quick access to actions * Important info always visible ### Trash Management Instead of permanent deletion, rules move to trash: **Move to trash:** 1. Select rule(s) 2. Click **Move to Trash** 3. Confirm action **What happens:** * Rule hidden from main table * Rule saved in trash for 30 days * Can restore rule anytime **Trash** button at top of table: **In trash you can:** * See all deleted rules * Restore rules (Restore) * Delete permanently (Delete Permanently) Rules in trash are automatically deleted after 30 days. Permanent deletion is irreversible! Restore rule from trash: 1. Enter trash (Trash button) 2. Select rule(s) to restore 3. Click **Restore** 4. Rule returns to main table **What's restored:** * All original settings * Status returns to original state * Dates remain as they were ### Organization by Priority **Priority** determines rule execution order: **Rules:** * **Lower** number = **Higher** priority * Priority 0 runs before Priority 10 * Rules with same Priority run by ID **Example:** | Priority | Rule Name | Execution Order | |----------|-----------|-----------------| | 0 | VIP 30% Discount | 1 (first) | | 5 | Regular 15% Discount | 2 | | 10 | Basic 5% Discount | 3 (last) | **Organization recommendations:** **VIP Layer (Priority 0-9):** * VIP customer discounts * Special promotions * Loyalty rules **General Layer (Priority 10-19):** * Regular promotions * Category discounts * BOGO and bundles **Base Layer (Priority 20+):** * Default discounts * Basic free shipping * General rules Leave gaps between Priority values (0, 10, 20) to have room to insert additional rules in future. ### Efficient Work Tips **Recommended name structure:** ``` [Date] - [Type] - [Details] ``` **Examples:** * ✅ "07/2024 - BOGO - Summer Shirts" * ✅ "Q3 - Free Shipping - Over $200" * ✅ "Hanukkah - 20% - Toys" **Benefits:** * Natural sorting by date * Quick identification of promotion type * Easy to find and manage **Using Draft:** * Rules in preparation * Future promotions * Rules for testing **Setting dates:** * Always set End date for temporary promotions * Use Start date for scheduled promotions * Check expired dates regularly **Every month:** * ✅ Delete expired rules * ✅ Check trash and empty it * ✅ Update Priority if needed **Every quarter:** * ✅ Review rule performance * ✅ Reorganize by priorities * ✅ Update internal documentation **Backup:** * Duplicate important rules * Document complex settings * Keep promotion history **Documentation:** * Note purpose of each rule * Document results * Learn from successes and failures ### Useful Keyboard Shortcuts | Action | Windows | Mac | |--------|---------|-----| | **Undo** | Ctrl+Z | Cmd+Z | | **Redo** | Ctrl+Y | Cmd+Shift+Z | | **Search** | Ctrl+K | Cmd+K | | **Save** (in modals) | Ctrl+S | Cmd+S | | **Close** (modal) | Esc | Esc | Use keyboard shortcuts to work faster and save time! ### Troubleshooting Common Issues **Check:** 1. ✅ Status is Active (not Draft) 2. ✅ Dates are correct (within current range) 3. ✅ Filters contain correct products 4. ✅ Conditions are met in cart 5. ✅ Priority not blocked by another rule **Solution:** 1. Check Priority - rule with lower Priority runs first 2. Change Filters so they don't overlap 3. Adjust Conditions to prevent conflict 4. Consider merging into one rule **Possible causes:** * Communication issue - check internet connection * Permission error - verify editing permissions * Session expired - log in again **Solution:** 1. Refresh page 2. Log in again 3. Try editing again ### Summary Proper management of discount rules requires: * 🎯 **Organization** - Clear names, organized Priority * 🔍 **Monitoring** - Periodic checking, cleanup * 📊 **Analysis** - Learning from results * 🛠️ **Tools** - Using Bulk Edit, Undo/Redo * 📝 **Documentation** - Recording and understanding rules Well-organized discount rules system = More successful promotions and easier management! ### Continue Reading

title: Discount Rule Types
description: Comprehensive guide to all available discount types in Whizmanage system
content: ## Discount Rule Types The Whizmanage system supports 7 different discount types, each tailored for a different purpose. Understanding the differences between types will help you choose the right tool for each promotion. ### Overview of All Types **Definition:** Direct discount on specific products **When to use:** * Discount on a specific category * Promotion on a specific brand * Discount by product attributes * General sale on product group **Examples:** * "20% off all electronics" * "$50 off shoes" * "30% off summer clothing" **Definition:** Discount on entire cart amount **When to use:** * General discount on entire purchase * "Over amount X get discount" promotion * Automatic coupon for all customers * Discount based on cart amount **Examples:** * "10% off entire cart" * "$100 off purchases over $500" * "15% off entire cart for Hanukkah" **Definition:** Tiered discounts based on purchase quantity **When to use:** * Encourage bulk purchases * Wholesale discounts * "The more you buy, the more you save" promotions * Quantity-based discount tiers **Examples:** * "Buy 3 items - 10% off, Buy 5 - 20% off" * "1-2 units: regular price, 3-5 units: 15% off" **Definition:** Buy X Get Y **from the same product** free/discounted **When to use:** * "Buy 2 Get 1 Free" * Promotions on single product * Encourage purchasing quantities of same item * Clearance promotions **Examples:** * "Buy 2 shirts, get 1 free" * "Buy 3 books, get 1 at 50% off" * "Buy 1 Get 1 Free" BOGO works only on the same product. If you want to buy product X and get a different product Y, use BXGY. **Definition:** Buy product(s) X and get **different** product(s) Y free/discounted **When to use:** * Cross-selling - selling complementary products * "Buy expensive product get cheap one free" * Bundle promotions * Encourage purchasing additional products **Examples:** * "Buy laptop get mouse free" * "Buy 2 shirts get pants at 50% off" * "Buy shampoo get conditioner free" **Definition:** Discount on shipping cost **When to use:** * Free shipping over amount * Discount on shipping for entire cart * Discounted shipping for specific products * Shipping promotions **Examples:** * "Free shipping over $200" * "50% off shipping" * "Free shipping on electronics" **Definition:** Bundle deals - Spend X get discount **When to use:** * "Spend $500 get $100 off" * "Bonus" promotions based on spending * Encourage cart size increase * Loyalty promotions **Examples:** * "Spend $300 get $50 off" * "Spend $1000 get $200 gift" *** ## Quick Comparison Table | Type | Main Purpose | Complexity | Best For | |------|--------------|------------|----------| | **Product Adjustment** | Discount on products | ⭐ | Simple promotions | | **Cart Adjustment** | Discount on cart | ⭐ | General coupons | | **Bulk Discount** | Tiered discounts | ⭐⭐ | Large quantities | | **BOGO** | Buy X Get Y (same product) | ⭐⭐ | BOGO promotions | | **BXGY** | Buy X Get Y (different product) | ⭐⭐⭐ | Cross-selling | | **Shipping** | Shipping discount | ⭐ | Free shipping | | **Spend Bundle** | Spend X Get Y | ⭐⭐ | Loyalty promotions | *** ## Summary Each discount type is designed for a different purpose. Choose the appropriate type for your promotion and enjoy easy and efficient management! ### Continue Reading

title: Introduction to Product Import
description: General overview of the product import system and its various capabilities
content: ## Introduction to the Import System Currently, the import system only supports importing via Google Sheets. Additional options such as importing from WooCommerce files and WhizManage will be added in future versions. The WhizManage import system allows you to easily import products from various sources, update existing products, and manage the import process in a controlled manner. The system supports multiple formats and interfaces to enable you to import and manage your products in the best possible way. ### Benefits of the Import System 1. **Import Flexibility** * Direct import from Google Sheets * Convenient access to the system from anywhere * Real-time product management 2. **Complete Control** * Two-way synchronization between the system and the file * Update product data in a familiar interface * Easy collaboration with your team 3. **Smart Data Integration** * Automatic product image import * Automatic category association * Automatic handling of product variations ### Supported Import Types {/* Options to be added in the future */} ### Recommended Work Approach 1. **Planning Ahead** * Prepare data in the appropriate format * Use the example file as a template * Perform a test import in a testing environment 2. **Using Advanced Features** * Leverage Google Sheets collaborative work options * Use spreadsheet formulas for automatic calculations * Set up conditional formatting to identify data issues 3. **Quality Control** * Review products after synchronization * Ensure all data was imported correctly * Maintain an up-to-date backup of product data For detailed information on the Google Sheets import process, including step-by-step instructions, see the Import from Google Sheets page.

title: Product Import Process
description: Comprehensive guide to the product import process in the WhizManage system
content: ## Product Import Process The WhizManage system allows importing products easily from various sources. Below is a detailed guide to the general import process. ### Supported Formats The system supports various formats for product import: | Format | File Extension | Notes | |--------|------------|--------| | **Excel** | .xlsx, .xls | Supports multiple sheets | | **CSV** | .csv | Recommended for maximum compatibility | | **ODS** | .ods | Open spreadsheet format | Use CSV format for maximum compatibility with other systems and to prevent data loss. ### How to Start the Import Process To open the import window: 1. Go to the product management screen 2. Find the "Import" button at the top of the screen (marked with a down arrow icon) 3. Click on the Import button In the import menu, you can choose between different options: 1. **WooCommerce File** - for importing CSV files from WooCommerce 2. **Google Sheets File** - for connecting and interfacing with Google Sheets 3. **WhizManage File** - for importing files from other WhizManage systems After selecting the import type, you'll need to choose the import mode: 1. **New Products** - for creating new products in the system 2. **Update Products** - for updating existing products in the system The import mode selection affects how product IDs and various fields are handled. After selecting the import type and mode: 1. Drag the import file to the designated area, or click to select a file 2. The system will check the file's validity 3. If the file is valid, you can proceed to the next step The system provides examples for each import type. Click on "Download Example File" below the drag area. After uploading the file: 1. Click on the "Start Import" button 2. The system will begin processing the file 3. A progress indicator will be displayed during processing ### Import Processing The system performs several automatic actions during file processing: 1. **File Structure Analysis** * Identifying columns and fields * Translating field names to the internal format * Checking field validity 2. **Image Processing** * Uploading product images from URLs * Creating image versions in different sizes * Associating images with the appropriate products 3. **Category and Tag Handling** * Identifying existing categories and tags * Creating new categories and tags * Associating products with the appropriate categories 4. **Product Attribute Handling** * Identifying existing attributes * Creating new attributes * Setting attribute values ### Import Review Table After file processing, in "New Products" mode, a review table will appear: The table allows: * Viewing products before final import * Editing data as needed * Removing products from the import * Filtering and searching products Use the editing functions in the table to correct incorrect or missing data before final import. ### Saving the Import After reviewing the table and editing the data: 1. Click on the "Save Import" button at the top of the screen 2. The system will begin the final import process 3. A progress indicator will display the process status 4. At the end of the process, a summary message will be displayed ### Tips for Successful Import 1. **File Preparation** * Use the example file as a template * Ensure all required fields are filled * Check the validity of image URLs 2. **Performing Import** * Start with a small file to test the process * Use a test environment before importing to the live site * Back up your system before large imports 3. **Solving Common Problems** * Character encoding issues: ensure the file is in UTF-8 encoding * Image upload problems: check URLs and access permissions * Field errors: check data compatibility with system requirements Importing products is an action that can affect your entire store. Always back up your system before performing a significant import.

title: Review and Edit Products Before Import
description: Guide for using the review and edit mode for products before final import into the system
content: ## Review and Edit Products Before Final Import One of the significant advantages of the WhizManage system is the ability to review and edit products before final import into the system. This mode allows you to make final adjustments, fix errors, and ensure everything looks correct before completing the process. ### Benefits of Review and Edit Mode The review mode allows: * Checking product data before final import * Identifying errors or missing information * Ensuring products meet your standards The editing interface offers: * Quick and convenient editing of product fields * Changing multiple products simultaneously * Preview of changes The editing interface offers advanced editing options not available in the regular import process. The preliminary approach saves: * Time on post-import corrections * Effort in identifying issues after product publication * Need for repeated imports ### How to Enter Review and Edit Mode The review and edit mode is activated automatically in some import processes: When selecting the "New Products" option during the import process: 1. The system will process the imported file 2. Automatically display the product review table 3. A special indicator will appear at the top of the screen indicating you are in review mode You can identify the review mode by: 1. A special alert message at the top of the screen 2. Changes in the product table interface 3. Appearance of "Import to Store" and "Cancel Import" buttons As long as you are in review mode, the products are not actually saved in the store. They will only be saved after clicking "Import to Store". ### Working in Review and Edit Mode The review table displays: 1. All products and variations from the imported file 2. Hierarchical structure of parent products and variations 3. All important columns for quick editing You can open variations of a product by clicking the arrow next to the parent product name. You can edit the following data: 1. Name, price, sale price 2. Description, stock, SKU 3. Attributes and options 4. Any other data appearing in the table Double-clicking on a cell in the table allows for quick editing of the value. In review mode, you can also: 1. Remove products you don't want to import 2. Change the order of products if needed 3. Add variations to existing products ### Completing the Import Process Before completing the import: 1. Perform a general review of all products 2. Ensure all data is accurate 3. Check that all images appear correctly After everything looks correct: 1. Click on the "Import to Store" button at the top of the screen 2. The system will begin the final import process 3. A progress indicator will be displayed during processing The final import process may take time depending on the number of products and images. Do not close the window during the process. After completing the import: 1. A confirmation message will be displayed 2. You'll receive a summary of the number of products imported 3. You'll be returned to the regular product management screen ### Canceling Import If for any reason you decide not to complete the import: 1. Click on the "Cancel Import" button at the top of the screen 2. The system will cancel the import process and delete the temporary data 3. You'll be returned to the product management screen without changes to the store data Canceling the import does not affect existing data in your store; it simply cancels the current import process. ### Advanced Tips for Review Mode 1. **Efficient Editing** * Use keyboard shortcuts for quick navigation in the table * Edit multiple rows simultaneously using multiple selection * Perform bulk actions on selected products 2. **Quality Control** * First check the most important products * Look for recurring patterns of errors * Use search and filter functions to find outlier values 3. **Data Preservation** * Review mode automatically saves changes * If a break is needed, you can return to review mode later * For safety, take screenshots of significant changes Although review mode allows many corrections, proper planning of the original file before import will save considerable time at this stage.

title: Import from Google Sheets
description: Guide for importing and synchronizing products using Google Sheets
content: ## Import Products from Google Sheets The WhizManage system allows you to manage products using Google Sheets efficiently and easily. ## New Features 🆕 * **Product Selection**: Choose which products appear in the file * **Category Filtering**: Quick filtering by categories * **ACF Fields**: Support for Advanced Custom Fields * **JetEngine Fields**: Support for custom JetEngine fields ## Benefits of Google Sheets Google Sheets allows: * Multiple users working simultaneously * Instant synchronization of changes * Version history and ability to revert to previous versions Data is available: * From any device with internet connection * No need to install software * High security with advanced permission options The familiar management interface allows: * Simple editing of product data * Using formulas for automatic calculations * Easy sorting and filtering of information ## Setting Up the File ### Product Selection 1. Navigate to Product Management 2. Click "Select Products for Import" 3. Use search and filtering for selection 4. Click "Save Settings" You can filter by categories and search by name or ID. ### Create Google Sheets File 1. Open the attached [example file](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/example) 2. Click "File" > "Make a copy" 3. Name the file identical to your website's URL (e.g., 'mystore.com') Matching the name to your domain is critical for automatic integration. 1. Click the "Share" button in the top corner 2. Set to "Anyone with the link can view" 3. Copy the displayed link 1. Look for a new "WhizManage" tab in the top menu 2. Click "WhizManage" > "Update File" 3. First time: authorize permissions for the script When authorizing, ensure you're logged into your Google account and trust the WhizManage application. ### Connect File to System In WhizManage system: 1. Navigate to Product Management 2. Click "Import" button 3. Select "Google Sheets file" option 1. Paste the copied link 2. Click "Check Connection" to verify validity 3. Click "Save Settings" to save connection Link format: `https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/[FILE_ID]/edit?usp=sharing` ## File Structure ### Basic Fields | Column Name | Description | Required | |-----------|--------|-------| | **Product Name** | Full product name | Yes | | **Price** | Regular product price | Yes | | **Sale Price** | Sale price (optional) | No | | **Main Image** | URL to main image | Yes | | **SKU** | Unique catalog number | No | | **Categories** | Categories separated by commas | No | | **Tags** | Tags separated by commas | No | | **Detailed Description** | Full product description | No | | **Short Description** | Product summary | No | | **Type** | Product type (simple, variable, etc.) | Yes | | **Status** | Product status (publish, draft, etc.) | No | | **Stock** | Available stock quantity | No | ### Custom Fields 🔧 The system supports custom fields: #### ACF / JetEngine Fields * **Auto-detection**: System automatically detects existing ACF fields * **Suffix**: Custom fields appear with suffix "(m)" * **Attributes**: Custom field attributes receive suffix "(a)" * **Field types**: Text, numbers, dates, boolean #### Structure Example | Product Name | Price | Color (a) | acf\_warranty (m) | jet\_brand (m) | |----------|------|-------------|-----------|----------| | iPhone 15 | 3999 | Silver | 24 months | Apple | | Samsung S24 | 3499 | Black | 18 months | Samsung | Custom fields are added automatically based on selected products. ### Product Variations For importing products with variations: 1. **Type column** with "variable product" value 2. **Attribute columns** with "(a)" suffix 3. **Variation rows** - each variation in separate row Parent product and variations must appear sequentially in the file. ## Data Synchronization After editing data in file: 1. Open Google Sheets file 2. Click "WhizManage" menu 3. Select "Update Site" option 4. Script automatically sends changes to site For reverse sync (site to file): 1. Open Google Sheets file 2. Click "WhizManage" menu 3. Select "Update File" option 4. Script pulls latest data from site Update file before significant editing to ensure you work with current data. ## Tips and Troubleshooting ### Organization and Backup * Use colors to classify products * Create periodic file copies * Use Google Sheets version history ### Common Errors * **"Cannot access file"**: Ensure file is shared for public viewing * **"ACF field not recognized"**: Verify field exists and is active * **"Product list not saved"**: Check internet connection Remember that changes in Google Sheets won't appear on site automatically until you run "Update Site".

title: Import from WhizManage Files
description: Guide for importing products from WhizManage system export files
content: ## Importing Products from WhizManage Files The WhizManage system enables easy and efficient transfer of products between different systems using dedicated export files. This option is ideal for synchronization between multiple stores, data backup, or transferring products between development and production environments. ### Benefits of Using WhizManage Files WhizManage export files offer: * Complete compatibility between different WhizManage systems * Preservation of all information without data loss * Precise transfer of all settings and parameters The product transfer process is simple and fast: * No need for data conversion * No need for manual adjustments * Minimum possible errors Use WhizManage files for product backup or copying products from a testing environment to a production environment. Option to use import for product updates: * Maintaining product IDs * Updating existing products and variations * Preserving relationships between products ### Preparing a WhizManage Export File 1. In the source system, navigate to the product management screen 2. Select the products you want to export or choose "All Products" 3. Click on the "Export" button (download icon) 4. Select "WhizManage File" from the menu 5. Save the created file to your computer You can use filters and search options to export only relevant products. Before importing, verify: 1. That product types are compatible between systems 2. That user permissions allow product importing 3. That there is enough storage space for products and images Check that the target system version is compatible with or newer than the source system version for maximum compatibility. ### Import Process in the Target System 1. In the target system, navigate to the product management screen 2. Click on the "Import" button (upload icon) 3. Select "WhizManage File" from the menu Choose the appropriate import type: 1. **New Products** - to create new products in the system 2. **Update Products** - to update existing products by ID or SKU Selecting "New Products" will create new copies even if similar products already exist in the system. 1. Drag the WhizManage file to the designated area or click to select a file 2. The system will check the file's validity 3. You'll receive a confirmation message if the file was accepted successfully After successfully uploading the file: 1. Click on the "Start Import" button 2. The system will begin processing the file 3. A progress indicator will be displayed during processing The import process may take time depending on the number of products and images in the file. ### What Does a WhizManage File Contain? A dedicated WhizManage file contains all the information required for complete product transfer, including: 1. **Basic Product Information** * Name, price, description * SKU, inventory, categories 2. **Advanced Information** * Product attributes and options * Variations and relationships between them * Tags and SEO settings 3. **Images and Media** * Links to product images * Product galleries and variation images * Downloadable files (if any) 4. **Relationships Between Products** * Related products * Upsell products * Grouped products A WhizManage file is a unique format specific to the WhizManage system and cannot be manually edited. Any changes may damage the file. ### Advanced Tips for Importing from WhizManage Files 1. **Creating Backups** * Back up the target system before significant imports * Keep copies of import files for documentation purposes * Document the import process and decisions made 2. **Importing in Stages** * For large systems, consider importing in small groups * First perform a test import with a few products * Arrange products by categories or types 3. **Post-Import Tests** * Check a representative sample of imported products * Verify that relationships between products are maintained * Check that images and media were uploaded properly When transferring an entire system to a new instance, start by importing system settings and templates before importing products.

title: Import from WooCommerce Files
description: Detailed guide for importing products from WooCommerce CSV files
content: ## Importing Products from WooCommerce Files The WhizManage system allows for smooth and simple importing of products from WooCommerce systems using CSV files. This feature is particularly useful when migrating from an existing WooCommerce store or when managing products simultaneously across multiple systems. ### Benefits of Importing from WooCommerce 1. **Full Compatibility** * Support for standard WooCommerce data structure * Automatic conversion of fields and column names * Preservation of relationships between products 2. **Complete Data Import** * Transfer of all product data including images and complex information * Support for product variations * Preservation of meta-data and custom information 3. **Flexibility** * Option to import new products or update existing ones * Selection of specific fields to import * Option to edit data before final import ### Preparing a CSV File from WooCommerce 1. In the WooCommerce admin interface, navigate to "Products" > "Export" 2. Select "Products" in the export menu 3. Choose the CSV format (default) 4. Define the fields to export or use the default settings 5. Click "Export" to download the file Choose "Export All Products" to include both regular products and variations in the export file. Before importing, verify that the file includes: 1. Valid column headers 2. Complete product data 3. Valid links to images 4. Variation information if relevant If the file is opened in a spreadsheet program, ensure you don't alter the original data structure when saving it again. ### Importing the File to WhizManage 1. Go to the product management screen in the WhizManage system 2. Click on the "Import" button (upload icon) 3. Select "WooCommerce File" from the menu You need to choose the appropriate import type: 1. **New Products** * For creating new products in the system * The system will ignore existing product IDs * Suitable for migrating from one system to another 2. **Update Products** * For updating existing products in the system * The system will identify products by ID or SKU * Suitable for synchronization or updating existing products 1. Drag the CSV file to the designated area or click to select a file 2. The system will check the file's compatibility 3. You'll receive a confirmation message if the file was accepted successfully If you're unsure about the required file structure, click on "Download Example File" to get a ready template. After successfully uploading the file: 1. Click on the "Start Creating Products" or "Start Updating Products" button (depending on the option you chose) 2. The system will begin processing the file 3. A progress indicator will be displayed during processing ### WooCommerce File Structure A standard WooCommerce file includes the following main columns: | Column | Description | Example | |-------|--------|--------| | **ID** | Unique product identifier | 123 | | **Type** | Product type | simple, variable, variation | | **SKU** | Unique catalog number | ABC-123 | | **Name** | Product name | Cotton Shirt | | **Published** | Publication status | 1 (yes) or 0 (no) | | **Regular price** | Regular price | 99.90 | | **Sale price** | Sale price | 79.90 | | **Categories** | Categories | Clothing, Shirts | | **Images** | Links to images | http://example.com/image.jpg | | **Attribute X name** | Attribute name | Color | | **Attribute X value(s)** | Attribute values | Red, Blue, Green | The WhizManage system automatically identifies columns even if they're in Hebrew, but it's recommended to use an English file for maximum compatibility. ### Handling Variations When importing products with variations: 1. **File Structure** * The parent product (`variable`) appears first * Followed by all variations (`variation`) * Variations are linked to the parent via the `Parent` field 2. **Attribute Handling** * `Attribute X name` columns define attribute names * `Attribute X value(s)` columns define the options * `Attribute X visible` columns define if the attribute is visible * `Attribute X global` columns define if the attribute is global ### Tips for Successful Import from WooCommerce 1. **File Preparation** * Maintain the original column structure * Ensure SKUs are unique * Verify that image links are valid and accessible 2. **During Import** * Start with a small import for testing * Pay attention to required fields * Use the review table to verify data accuracy 3. **Troubleshooting Common Issues** * Character encoding issues: ensure the file is in UTF-8 encoding * Attribute issues: check the structure and format of attribute values * Product relationships: ensure correct order of parent products and variations Complex imports with hundreds of products and variations may take a long time. Do not close the window or refresh the page during the process.

title: Installation
description: The following guide covers the process of installing the plugin and how to initially configure it to get started
content: ## Installing the WhizManage Plugin The WhizManage plugin is installed similarly to any other WordPress plugin. Below is a simple guide for installing the system and activating it. There are two ways to download and install the WhizManage plugin: **Option 1: Install directly from the WordPress admin interface** 1. Log in to your WordPress admin area 2. Go to "Plugins" > "Add New" 3. In the search box, type "WhizManage" 4. When the plugin appears in the list, click "Install Now" **Option 2: Download from the WhizManage website and install manually** 1. Visit the [WhizManage](https://whizmanage.com) website 2. Go to the downloads page and download the plugin ZIP file 3. In your WordPress admin, go to "Plugins" > "Add New" 4. Click "Upload Plugin" at the top of the screen 5. Select the downloaded ZIP file and click "Install Now" 1. After installation, click "Activate Plugin" 2. The WhizManage plugin will be added to the WordPress sidebar menu 3. Click on "WhizManage" in the sidebar menu to enter the plugin management interface After the initial activation, the WhizManage plugin is available in the basic (free) version with certain limitations on functionality. If you've purchased one of the Pro versions of WhizManage: 1. Make sure you've received the license code by email after purchase (You can also find the license in your personal area on the [WhizManage](https://whizmanage.com) website) 2. title: Initial Settings
description: Guide for configuring the system after installation, including customizing the user interface and product table
content: ## Initial Settings After installing and activating the WhizManage plugin, you can customize the system according to your personal preferences. This guide will help you configure the interface to suit your needs. ### Choosing a Theme WhizManage allows you to choose between different themes for the user interface: 1. Click on your user image in the top corner of the interface 2. In the dropdown menu, select "Theme" 3. Choose one of the following options: * **Light** - interface with light colors * **Dark** - interface with dark colors * **System** - automatic adjustment according to your system settings The theme change takes effect immediately and is saved automatically - no need to click "Save". ### Customizing the Product Table The product table is the heart of the system and can be fully customized to suit your needs: 1. Open the main product table 2. Click the "+" (plus) button in the top corner of the table 3. In the window that opens, you can: * Check or uncheck columns to show/hide them * Change the order of columns by dragging and dropping within the window * Filter columns using the "Find column to show/hide" search field 4. After making your desired changes, click "Save as default" to save the settings for future use Clicking "Save as default" will save the current column configuration as your default setting. If you want to return to the original settings, you can click "Reset Table". In addition to the settings window, you can make further adjustments directly in the table: 1. **Change column width** - drag the border between column headers to change the column width 2. **Change column order** - drag the column header to the desired position 3. **Quick column hiding** - click the small arrow next to the column header and select "Hide" 4. **Table sorting** - click on a column header to sort by that column, or click the small arrow and select "Asc" (ascending) or "Desc" (descending) These changes are automatically saved for the current user. However, to save the changes permanently as default, remember to click the "Save as default" button in the column settings window. You can adjust the number of products displayed on each page of the table: 1. At the bottom of the table, find the rows per page selector 2. Choose the desired number from the dropdown list (typically options are 10, 25, 50, 100) 3. The selection is saved automatically and will apply to the table immediately ### Testing and Further Customization After completing the initial settings, it's recommended to perform a brief test of the system: 1. Verify that all products are properly displayed in the table 2. Try editing a simple product to test the editing functionality 3. Try creating a new product (available in all versions) 4. Test the filtering and search functionality in the table In the basic (free) version, some features are limited. Features available only in Pro versions include: advanced variation editing, bulk product editing, spreadsheet-style editing, custom fields, advanced filtering, and more. ## Features Available in Different Versions Below is a list of features not included in the basic free version: * Add product variations * Add new product with advanced features * Drag & drop columns * Edit All - Like in spreadsheets * Bulk editing * Add and edit customized fields * Full support * Personalized columns * Advanced filters * New features as added For more information about the features available in each version and upgrade options, visit the [WhizManage](https://whizmanage.com) website or contact support at support@whizmanage.com.

title: Product Attributes and Their Configuration
description: Explanation of different attribute types in the system and how to configure them
content: ## What is a Product Attribute? A product attribute is a characteristic that defines different aspects of your product. The system supports two main types of attributes, each serving different purposes. ### Types of Attributes Product attributes are specific to an individual product. **When to Use:** * When the attribute is unique to this product * When there's no need to share with other products * When maximum flexibility is required **Common Examples:** * Storage capacity in mobile phones * Frame material in glasses * Engine type in vehicles Global attributes are shared across multiple products and enable standardization. **When to Use:** * When the same attribute appears in multiple products * When maintaining consistency across the store * When filtering and searching by attribute is required **Common Examples:** * Clothing sizes (S, M, L) * Standard colors * Common materials ### Choosing the Right Attribute Type | Criterion | Product Attribute | Global Attribute | |-----------|------------------|------------------| | Reusability | Not Required | Required | | Flexibility | Maximum | Limited | | Maintenance | Simple | More Complex | ## Creating New Attributes ### Attribute Addition Process * Locate the product you want to add variations to in the products table * Switch the row to edit mode * Find the "Type" column * Ensure it's set to "Variable Product" (variations product) * Next to the "Variable Product" setting, there's a variations management button * Click the button to open the variations management window * Click "Add Attribute" * Choose the appropriate attribute type * Select an existing attribute, or create a new one ## Best Practices 1. **Plan Ahead** * Define attributes before adding products * Consider uniform structure for each category 2. **Maintain Consistency** * Use global attributes when possible * Keep names consistent and structure proper 3. **Documentation** * Document attribute usage * Perform periodic reviews to identify duplications Take time to plan your attribute structure as it significantly impacts both store management and customer experience.

title: Creating Product Variations
description: A step-by-step guide to creating product variations in the system
content: ## Creating Product Variations Creating product variations is a streamlined process that automatically generates all possible combinations of your product attributes and options. ### Before You Begin Before creating variations, ensure you have: 1. Added all necessary attributes to your product 2. Defined the options for each attribute 3. Decided which attributes you want to include ### Setting Up Attribute Options For each attribute: 1. Add all required options using either: * Product attribute options * Global attribute terms 2. Consider using "Any" option when: * All options have the same price * No separate inventory tracking is needed * No separate images are required ### Generating Variations Once your attributes and options are set up: 1. Click the "Generate Variations" button 2. The system will automatically: * Create all possible combinations * Generate unique IDs for each variation * Set default values for price and stock For example, with: * Color: Red, Blue * Size: S, M, L The system will create 6 variations (2 colors × 3 sizes) After generation, all variations appear in a table showing: * Variation attributes combination * Regular price * Sale price * Stock status * Menu order Review all generated variations to ensure they match your product requirements.

title: Introduction to Product Variations
description: A comprehensive introduction to the product variations management system
content: ## Introduction Product variations management is one of the most crucial components in running an online store. The system enables you to create different versions of the same basic product, such as different sizes and colors, while maintaining separate inventory tracking for each variation. ### What Are Product Variations? Product variations allow you to offer the same product in multiple different versions. For example: * A shirt in various colors and sizes * A phone with different storage capacities * Glasses with different frame colors ### Benefits of Using Variations 1. **Efficient Inventory Management** * Separate tracking for each product version * Automated inventory alerts * Detailed reports for each variation 2. **Enhanced User Experience** * Intuitive selection interface * Clear presentation of all options * Prevention of confusion between different versions 3. **Pricing Flexibility** * Ability to set different prices for each variation * Special offers for specific variations * Dynamic pricing based on product attributes ### System Structure The variations system consists of several key components: ### System Architecture Our variations system is built for: 1. **Scalability** - Handle thousands of variations effortlessly 2. **Flexibility** - Adapt to any product type 3. **Performance** - Quick loading and smooth operation ### Getting Started Before creating variations, consider: 1. The key features that distinguish your products 2. How many variations you'll need 3. Your inventory management requirements Start with a simple structure and expand as needed. It's easier to add variations later than to simplify a complex structure. To begin using the variations system: 1. Choose your product attributes 2. Define your options 3. Create your first variations Plan your variation structure carefully as it can affect your store's performance and user experience.

title: Managing Existing Variations
description: Guide to managing existing product variations in the system
content: ## Managing Existing Variations The variations table displays all existing variations for the product: | Column | Description | Example | |--------|------------|---------| | **Attributes** | Combination of variation attributes | Red / M | | **Regular Price** | Regular price of the variation | $99.90 | | **Sale Price** | Sale price if exists | $79.90 | | **Description** | Variation-specific description | | | **Menu Order** | Display order in shop | 1 | For each variation, you can edit: 1. **Prices** * Regular price * Sale price 2. **Additional Information** * Variation description * Display order in shop Changes are only saved after clicking the "Save Changes" button. You can delete variations that are no longer needed: 1. The variation will be removed from the variations list 2. Deleted variations cannot be recovered 3. Deletion takes effect only after saving changes Make sure you really want to delete the variation before confirming deletion.

title: Managing Product Options
description: A comprehensive guide to managing product options and understanding the Any mode
content: ## Understanding Options Management Options are the specific values available for each product attribute. Effective options management is crucial for creating a clear and organized product structure. Product attribute options are specific to individual products: | Feature | Description | |---------|-------------| | **Product Specificity** | Options are unique to the current product | | **Flexibility** | Complete freedom in naming and structuring options | | **Management** | Simple, direct, without affecting other products | #### Adding New Product Options 1. Click the edit button (pencil icon) next to the desired attribute 2. Enter the new option name 3. Click "Add" Global attribute options are managed centrally: | Feature | Description | |---------|-------------| | **Centralization** | Options are managed centrally and shared across products | | **Standardization** | Consistency across all products using the attribute | | **Maintenance** | Central updates affect all products using the option | #### Adding New Global Options 1. Click the edit button next to the global attribute 2. Choose one of two methods: * Select from existing terms list * Create a new term in the global library ## The "Any" Mode "Any" mode is a unique feature that provides maximum flexibility in options management. #### When to Use Any Mode: | Use Case | Description | |----------|-------------| | **Uniform Pricing** | When all options are sold at the same price | | **Shared Inventory** | When separate inventory tracking isn't needed | | **Simple Display** | When different images aren't needed for each option | 1. **Simplified Management** * Fewer variations to manage * Faster updates * Reduced error potential 2. **Enhanced User Experience** * Simpler selection interface * Faster page loading * Less confusion in purchase process Use Any mode when you want to offer multiple options without the complexity of full variation management. 1. **Pricing Constraints** * Cannot set different prices for different options * Cannot apply specific discounts to certain options 2. **Inventory Management** * No separate inventory tracking per option * Limited ability to manage specific option alerts 3. **Display Limitations** * Cannot show different images per option * Limited ability to display option-specific information Consider these limitations when deciding whether to use Any mode for your products.
